source.text: ἐλθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν οὐκ ἀφῆκεν εἰσελθεῖν τινα σὺν αὐτῷ εἰ μὴ Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ τὸν πατέρα τῆς παιδὸς καὶ τὴν μητέρα.

records.literal_gloss: Having come then into the house, not he allowed to go in anyone with him except Peter and John and James and the father of the child and the mother.

en.L: And having come into the house, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not allow anyone to go in with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} except Peter and John and James, and the father of the child and the mother.
en.B: Arriving at the house, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} allowed only Peter, John and James, and the girl's father and mother, to go in with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus came to the house. He let only Peter, John, James, and the girl's parents go inside with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: to go in with him: into the room where the girl lay
decisions.reason: Mourners were already in the house (8:52-53). Mark 5:40 says Jesus put them out and went in where the child was.

decisions.choice: the child: the girl
decisions.reason: The word can mean a child or a servant. Here it is the daughter (8:42, 54).

decisions.choice: Peter, John and James: three disciples who are with Jesus at key moments
decisions.reason: The same three go up the mountain with him in 9:28, where Luke again names John before James.

decisions.choice: the girl's parents
alternatives: the father of the child and the mother
decisions.reason: Readable uses one word for both.

source.text: ἔκλαιον δὲ πάντες καὶ ἐκόπτοντο αὐτήν.

records.literal_gloss: Were weeping then all and mourning her.

en.L: And all were weeping and mourning for her.
en.B: Everyone was crying and wailing for her.
en.R: Everyone there was crying and grieving loudly for the girl.

decisions.choice: mourning: beating the breast in loud grief
decisions.reason: The verb means to beat oneself in grief. Mourning for the dead was loud and public, and sometimes mourners were hired (Jeremiah 9:17-18; Matthew 9:23).

decisions.choice: all: the people gathered at the house
decisions.reason: These are the mourners, not the five who went in with Jesus.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Μὴ κλαίετε, οὐ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν ἀλλὰ καθεύδει.

records.literal_gloss: But he said: Not weep, not for she died but sleeps.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Do not weep, for she did not die, but she is sleeping."
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them, "Do not weep. She has not died. She is sleeping."
en.R: But Jesus said, "Stop crying! She is not dead. She is only sleeping."

decisions.choice: she did not die but is sleeping: her death is like a sleep from which Jesus will wake her
decisions.reason: Luke says plainly that she had died (8:49, 53, 55). Jesus speaks of death as sleep because he is about to wake her, as with Lazarus (John 11:11-14). Scripture often speaks of death as sleep (Daniel 12:2; 1 Thessalonians 4:13).

decisions.choice: do not weep: stop weeping
decisions.reason: The command tells them to stop the weeping already going on.

decisions.choice: only
decisions.reason: Readable adds "only" to bring out the contrast with death.

source.text: καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ, εἰδότες ὅτι ἀπέθανεν.

records.literal_gloss: And they were laughing at him, knowing that she died.

en.L: And they were laughing at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, knowing that she had died.
en.B: They ridiculed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, since they knew that she had died.
en.R: They laughed at Jesus, because they knew the girl was dead.

decisions.choice: laughing at: mocking, laughing with scorn
decisions.reason: The verb means to laugh someone down. They think Jesus's words are foolish.

decisions.choice: knowing that she had died: they were certain
decisions.reason: Their scorn confirms that the girl had truly died. Jesus is about to raise the dead (7:22).

source.text: αὐτὸς δὲ κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς ἐφώνησεν λέγων· Ἡ παῖς, ἔγειρε.

records.literal_gloss: But he having taken hold of the hand of her called out saying: The child, arise.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, taking hold of her hand, called out, saying, "Child, arise!"
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took hold of her hand and called, "Child, get up!"
en.R: But Jesus took the girl's hand and called out, "Child, get up!"

decisions.choice: But he, taking hold: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: But he, having put them all outside and taking hold, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add that he put everyone outside, which matches Mark 5:40. Early manuscripts lack the words. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: arise: get up, rise
decisions.reason: The verb is used for getting up and for being raised from the dead (7:14, 22; 9:22).

decisions.choice: taking hold of her hand: touching the dead
decisions.reason: Touching a dead body made a person unclean (Numbers 19:11). Jesus touches the dead girl, as he touched the bier of the widow's son (7:14), and gives life.

source.text: καὶ ἐπέστρεψεν τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτῆς, καὶ ἀνέστη παραχρῆμα, καὶ διέταξεν αὐτῇ δοθῆναι φαγεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And returned the spirit of her, and she rose up immediately, and he directed to her to be given to eat.

en.L: And her spirit returned, and she rose up immediately, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} directed that [something] be given to her to eat.
en.B: Her spirit came back to her, and she rose at once, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave orders that she be given food.
en.R: Her life came back into her, and she got up right away. Jesus told them to give her some food.

decisions.choice: her spirit: her breath of life
decisions.reason: The word means spirit or breath. Her life returned to her body.

decisions.choice: her spirit returned: as when Elijah raised the widow's son
decisions.reason: When Elijah prayed, the boy's life came back into him and he lived (1 Kings 17:21-22). Luke has already linked Jesus with Elijah's miracle (4:25-26; 7:15).

decisions.choice: something to eat: proof that she was truly alive and well
decisions.reason: She is not a ghost or half alive. She can eat, as the risen Jesus will (24:41-43).

decisions.choice: Her life
decisions.reason: Readable says what "spirit" means here, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτῆς· ὁ δὲ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν τὸ γεγονός.

records.literal_gloss: And were amazed the parents of her; but he instructed them no one to tell the [thing] having happened.

en.L: And her parents were amazed; but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} instructed them to tell no one what had happened.
en.B: Her parents were beside themselves with amazement. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} charged them to keep what had happened to themselves.
en.R: Her parents were so amazed! But Jesus ordered them to keep it to themselves. They were not to tell anyone about it.

decisions.choice: were amazed: were astonished, beside themselves
decisions.reason: The verb means to be out of one's mind with wonder.

decisions.choice: to tell no one: a command Luke gives without a reason
alternatives: a command to lie about it
decisions.reason: Jesus gave similar orders after other healings and about who he was (5:14; 9:21). Luke does not explain the order here.
